slides.title: Misc 1 Gemma 2B with 10M context runs
slides.text: Misc 1 Gemma 2B with 10M context runs in less than 32GB memory The largest bottleneck (in terms of memory) for LLMs is the KV cache. It grows quadratically in multi-head attention The "InfiniAttention" splits the attention in local attention blocks. Those local attention blocks are taken and apply recurrence to the local attention blocks for the final result of 10M context global attention. A lot of the inspiration for our ideas comes from the Transformer-XL paper. https://twitter.com/rohanpaul_ai/status/1796137219712754118 https://github.com/mustafaaljadery/gemma-2B-10M Andrew Ng A barrier to faster progress in generative AI is evaluations (evals). Would adding a fact-checking agent improve the results? https://twitter.com/AndrewYNg/status/1796206876805489105 https://www.deeplearning.ai/the-batch/issue-251/ Yann LeCun What I and many (most) people at FAIR have working is no mystery. We call it AMI (Advanced Machine Intelligence). Objective-Driven AI, JEPA, world models, planning/reasoning is part of that. - https://twitter.com/ylecun/status/1794249923329720415 Xai (owned by Elon Musk) is working on new modes for its chatbot Grok: Socrates  & DEI (Diversity Equity and Inclusion) . OpenAI - GPT-4o available via API Google AI Overviews = AI-generated answers -  are now appearing in around 11% of queries (down from around 27% when the feature was launched last month. slides.title: Misc 2 Thought-Augmented Reasoning with LLMs Buffer of
slides.text: Misc 2 Thought-Augmented Reasoning with LLMs Buffer of Thoughts - containing high-level thoughts distilled from problem-solving processes. Using this buffer enhances  the accuracy, efficiency, and robustness of LLM-based reasoning. It demonstrates SOTA performance on 10 challenging tasks while requiring 12% of the cost of multi-query prompting methods like Tree-of-Thoughts. https://twitter.com/omarsar0/status/1799113545696567416 https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04271 Scalable MatMul-free Language Modeling https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.02528 MatMul (Matrix Multiplication) operations can be completely eliminated from LLMs while maintaining strong performance MatMul-free models achieve performance on-par with state-of-the-art Transformers We provide a GPU-efficient implementation of this model which reduces memory usage A custom hardware solution on an FPGA used to process billion-parameter scale models at 13W beyond human readable throughput, moving LLMs closer to brain-like efficiency Claude can now use tools https://www.anthropic.com/news/tool-use-ga

slides.title: Milvus Lite - Easy to Use Local Vector
slides.text: Milvus Lite - Easy to Use Local Vector DB Milvus Lite https://milvus.io/docs/milvus_lite.md # pip install "pymilvus>=2.4.2" from pymilvus import MilvusClient client = MilvusClient("mydb_file.db") Till a few months ago, Prompt Engineering was all the hype . The entire job market was filled with the role of prompt engineers, but not so anymore . People even wrote books/blogs like the Top 50 prompts to get the best of GPT, so on and so forth. But large-scale experiments have clearly shown that there is no single prompt or strategy that works for all kinds of problems, it’s just some prompts appear to be better in isolation but are a hit-and-miss when analyzed comprehensively. DSPy (Declarative Self-Improving Pipelines) is a framework developed by Stanford University that aims to simplify and streamline the process of building language model (LLM) pipelines. https://medium.com/aiguys/prompt-engineering-is-dead-dspy-is-new-paradigm-for-prompting-c80ba3fc4896 DSPy - express LLM tasks in a high-level, declarative manner, similar to PyTorch. Self-Improving Pipelines - automatically optimize LLM calls over time Modularity - LLMs are treated as modules Easy to use, Pythonic syntax and intuitive APIs. DSPy: Prompt Engineering Is Dead import dspy turbo = dspy.OpenAI(model='gpt-3.5-turbo') colbertv2_wiki17_abstracts = dspy.ColBERTv2(url='http://somedomain/wiki17_abstracts') dspy.settings.configure(lm=turbo, rm=colbertv2_wiki17_abstracts) # ...

slides.text: Right to Warn AI researchers demand "Right to Warn" Current and former employees from top AI labs, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and DeepMind just published an open letter This letter was also supported by Yoshua Bengio, Geoffrey Hinton, and Stuart Russell They push AI companies to provide whistleblower protection so that workers can warn about potential AI dangers without fear of retaliation. Eliminating non-disparagement clauses concerning AI risk Establishing and facilitating anonymous channels for raising concerns Expanding whistleblower protections and anti-retaliation measures Qwen2 from Alibaba Cloud 5 sizes (0.5B, 1.5B, 7B, 57B-14B MoE, 72B) Base & Instruct versions Open source (Apache 2.0) except 72B. Models are multilingual in 29 languages https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen2 https://huggingface.co/spaces/Qwen/Qwen2-72B-Instruct https://qwenlm.github.io/blog/qwen2/ https://ollama.com/library/qwen2 Models achieve SOTA performance on academic and chat benchmarks Qwen2-72B: MMLU 82.3, IFEval 77.6, MT-Bench 9.12, HumanEval 86.0 Qwen2-7B: MMLU 70.5, MT-Bench 8.41, HumanEval 79.9. slides.title: Automated Knowledge Graph Construction with LLMs Automating knowledge
slides.text: Automated Knowledge Graph Construction with LLMs Automating knowledge graph construction with LLMs Knowledge graphs are networks that represent data in a graphical format. Difficulties of constructing them include the time and cost, as well as the fact that different graphs are needed for different domains. LLMs can be used to extract knowledge from text. Researchers are exploring ways to combine LLMs and knowledge graphs. This could improve the accuracy of both knowledge graphs and LLMs. https://medium.com/@researchgraph/automated-knowledge-graph-construction-with-large-language-models-150512d1bc22 LlamaIndex - Property Graph Index : A Powerful New Way to Build Knowledge Graphs with LLMs https://www.llamaindex.ai/blog/introducing-the-property-graph-index-a-powerful-new-way-to-build-knowledge-graphs-with-llms from llama_index.indices.property_graph \ import SchemaLLMPathExtractor entities = Literal[ "PERSON", "PLACE", "THING" ] relations = Literal[ "PART_OF", "HAS", "IS_A" ] schema = {"PERSON": [ "PART_OF", "HAS", "IS_A" ], "PLACE": [ "PART_OF", "HAS" ], "THING": [ "IS_A" ]} kg_extractor = SchemaLLMPathExtractor( llm=llm, possible_entities=entities, possible_relations=relations, kg_validation_schema=schema, strict=True)

slides.title: Architectures in Agentic Systems Architectures in Agentic Systems
slides.text: Architectures in Agentic Systems Architectures in Agentic Systems https://x.com/alexalbert__/status/1796211969432887331 Delegation : Use cheaper, faster models for cost and speed gains. Example: Opus delegates to Haiku. Parallelization : Cut latency (but not cost) by running agents in parallel. Debate : Multiple agents with different roles engage in discussion to reach better decisions. Example - software engineer, security engineer, product manager, final agent Specialization : A generalist agent orchestrates, while specialists execute tasks. Tool Suite Experts : When using 100s or 1000s of tools, specialize agents in tool subsets.
